title: Membrane contact explains the higher synapse counts of two-way connections in 7 C. elegans nerve rings; in 2 fly connectomes a 1.2 to 1.3 fold excess stays after coarse controls
abstract: Question: are two-way (reciprocal) connections stronger than one-way connections only because large neurons and neurons that touch more make more synapses in both directions? Approach: we fit log synapse count on a two-way indicator with presynaptic and postsynaptic neuron fixed effects and dyadic-robust errors. We added membrane contact area (7 C. elegans nerve rings from Witvliet et al. 2021), cell-type pairs, dominant neuropil and a neuropil-overlap proxy (FlyWire v783 and hemibrain v1.2). Results: in the worm, two-way connections had 1.22 times more synapses with neuron effects only (pooled 95% CI 1.17 to 1.27). Two-way pairs had 2.08 times more contact. With contact as a control, the ratio was 0.95 (0.91 to 0.99), and all 7 animals from birth to adult agreed. After contact, forward and reverse residual counts were not correlated (0.04, CI -0.03 to 0.10; 0.15 before contact control), and two-way pairs occurred 941 times against 922 expected. In the fly, at 5 or more synapses, two-way connections stayed 1.23 (FlyWire) and 1.33 (hemibrain) times stronger with neuron and neuropil effects, 1.22 to 1.30 within cell-type pairs, and 1.24 and 1.32 with the neuropil-overlap proxy. Both hemispheres agreed. Fly forward and reverse residuals correlated at 0.13 to 0.26, similar to the worm before contact control. Cholinergic pairs had the smallest fly excess (1.09). A mouse MICrONS sample had only 7 two-way pairs and gave no conclusion. Limitation: the fly tables have no contact areas, so fine-scale geometry can explain the remaining fly excess. Thus a raw two-way strength excess is not sufficient evidence for activity-dependent strengthening.

display.caption: C. elegans nerve ring, 8 animals. (A) Synapse-count ratio of two-way to one-way connections with 95% dyadic-robust CIs under four models: no control, neuron fixed effects, plus contact-area bins, plus ordered neuron-class pair. Dataset 7 has no contact table. (B) Two-way pairs have about 2 times more membrane contact after neuron effects. The contact control removes the strength excess.

Drosophila FlyWire v783 and hemibrain v1.2. Synapse-count ratio of two-way to one-way connections at several thresholds, with neuron, dominant-neuropil, cell-type-pair and neuropil-overlap controls. The ratio stays at 1.2 to 1.45 under every available control. These tables have no membrane contact areas.

(A) Spearman correlation of forward and reverse residual log synapse counts in two-way pairs. In the worm, contact control takes it from 0.15 to 0.04. The fly values (0.13 to 0.26) are like the worm value before contact control. (B) FlyWire ratio by predicted transmitter pair: smallest for ACh-to-ACh pairs.
